# Equal endpoint volumes in every dimension: a proved surplus window and a width-bound gap

This note concerns exactly three positive-volume fibers at integer bases
-1,0,1. It proves a dimension-uniform regime for the actual two-center
method using g_((A+B)/2) and g_K. It also certifies that the available
residual and support-width estimates, even with exact directional widths,
do not close the remaining regime. The latter is a failure of those
estimates, not a counterexample to the depth theorem or to either center.

## 1. The actual three-fiber theorem

Let d>=1 and let A,K,B be d-dimensional convex bodies with

    |A|=|B|=a>0, M=(A+B)/2 subset K, m=|M|, k=|K|,
    1<=m/a<=11/8.

Let Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d and put

    delta_d=(-57+202Gamma-121Gamma^2)/64>0,
    c_d=2Gamma+delta_d,
    eta_d=Gamma c_d/(c_d+2Gamma)>Gamma/2.                         (1)

In the actual mixed set

    S=({-1} x A) union ({0} x K) union ({1} x B),

the deterministic choice

    y=(0,g_M) if k/a<=c_d/Gamma,
    y=(0,g_K) otherwise                                           (2)

has normalized halfspace depth at least eta_d. Thus it satisfies the
n=1 OC bound in every continuous dimension under this one stated
Minkowski-volume restriction. The restriction is essential to the proof;
this is not the unrestricted conjecture.

Every such triple is realizable as the three fibers of the convex hull
of those three lifted bodies. Indeed midpoint compatibility ensures
that convex combinations contributing at base zero do not enlarge K;
the endpoint fibers stay A,B, and the projection is [-1,1].

## 2. An exact all-dimensional residual estimate

For u!=0 and arbitrary t, let P be the sum of the endpoint volumes in

    {u.x>=u.g_M+t} on A, {u.x>=u.g_M-t} on B.

Write r=m/a. Then

    P/a >= [1-{2[(1-Gamma)r]^(1/d)-1}^d]_+.                      (3)

Here is the complete proof. If P>=a there is nothing to prove. Otherwise
both residual bodies have positive volumes a-U,a-V, where U+V=P<a.
Their midpoint lies in the residual halfspace through g_M. Ordinary
Grunbaum bounds that residual volume by (1-Gamma)m, and ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski gives

    (a-U)^(1/d)+(a-V)^(1/d)<=2[(1-Gamma)m]^(1/d).

For two numbers in [0,a] with sum 2a-P, their root sum is minimized
at the endpoints (a,a-P), by concavity of x^(1/d). Consequently
1+(1-P/a)^(1/d)<=2[(1-Gamma)r]^(1/d), proving (3).
All continuous halfspace boundaries have zero d-volume. Closed residual
bodies are therefore legitimate, including tangent or saturated cuts.

The elementary bounds

    4/11<Gamma<=1/2                                               (4)

hold in every d>=1. The upper bound follows from (1+1/d)^d>=2.
The lower follows from (1+1/d)^d<e and e<11/4. For a direct rational
bound, the exponential series through degree three gives
e<8/3+(1/24)/(1-1/5)=87/32<11/4.

For 1<=r<=11/8 set x=[(1-Gamma)r]^(1/d). Then

    1/2<=x<1,
    2x-1<=x^2,
    (1-Gamma)r<7/8.

The first lower bound follows from (1-Gamma)r>=1/2 and d>=1.
The upper bound and the last bound follow from (4). Raising the middle
inequality to the positive integer d in (3) yields the simpler bound

    P/a>=1-(1-Gamma)^2r^2.                                       (5)

The difference between (5) and Gamma(2-r) is the concave quadratic

    D_Gamma(r)=1-(1-Gamma)^2r^2-Gamma(2-r).

At r=1 it equals Gamma(1-Gamma); at r=11/8 it equals delta_d in (1).
The latter is the smaller endpoint value, because

    64[delta_d-Gamma(1-Gamma)]
       =-57+138Gamma-57Gamma^2<0  for 4/11<=Gamma<=1/2.

Indeed the polynomial is increasing on this interval and has value
-9/4 at Gamma=1/2. Also the polynomial defining 64delta_d is concave
in Gamma, so its minimum on [4/11,1/2] occurs at an endpoint. Those
endpoint values are 55/121 and 55/4, respectively. In particular

    delta_d>=55/7744>0.

Concavity of D_Gamma now proves

    P/a>=Gamma(2-r)+delta_d.                                     (6)

## 3. All ambient halfspaces and the actual source switch

Move any containing halfspace parallel until its boundary passes through
(0,g_M); this cannot increase its captured measure. If its continuous
normal is nonzero, its own K trace contains the corresponding M cap,
whose volume is at least Gamma m. Adding (6) gives raw mass at least

    Gamma m+P >=(2Gamma+delta_d)a=c_d a.                         (7)

If its continuous normal is zero, the closed through-source halfspace
contains K and one entire endpoint, of mass k+a>=2a. This is larger
than c_d a: on [4/11,1/2], delta_d<=55/256 and 2Gamma<=1, so c_d<2.
Thus the purely integer case and its positive boundary mass are included.
The point g_M belongs to M subset K.

At the other actual point (0,g_K), ordinary Grunbaum on K alone gives
raw depth at least Gamma k; purely integer halfspaces capture all of K.
Hence the maximum over these two fixed candidates is at least

    max(c_d a,Gamma k)/(k+2a).

As a function of k/a the first ratio decreases and the second increases.
They meet at k/a=c_d/Gamma, with value eta_d in (1), proving both the
choice (2) and the theorem. No centroid of a Minkowski sum is replaced
by the mean of the endpoint centroids.

## 4. The directional support-width estimate and its exact scope

For arbitrary equal-volume endpoints, write w_A,w_B for their widths
under u. Since width(M)=(w_A+w_B)/2, the elementary centroid support
distance bound gives

    h_M(u)-u.g_M >=(w_A+w_B)/[2(d+1)].

For clarity, that bound follows by projecting a convex body onto [0,1].
Homothety from a point at its minimum shows its projection CDF is at
least s^d. Integrating the complement gives projected mean at most
d/(d+1), the desired support-distance estimate.

The two endpoint cap heights delta_A,delta_B sum to at least
(w_A+w_B)/(d+1). Supporting-point homotheties put at least
a clamp(delta_A/w_A,0,1)^d and its B analogue in the captured sets.
If either ratio reaches one, its full volume already exceeds the bound
below. Otherwise replace negative ratios by zero and apply Holder.
For d>1 this gives the exact direction-specific lower estimate

    P/a >= W_d(R):=
      (R+1)^d/[(d+1)^d(R^(d/(d-1))+1)^(d-1)], R=w_A/w_B.          (8)

No proper-cut assumption is used. In particular W_d(1)=2/(d+1)^d.

For d>=2, actual sectional Brunn--Minkowski gives a volume control on
the ratio:

    R+R^(-1)<=2^d r-2.                                          (9)

To prove (9), normalize both projection intervals to the parameter
s in [0,1]. If f(s),g(s) are the corresponding (d-1)-section volumes,
their section sums occur in A+B at parameter (w_A+w_B)s. Their
(d-1)-volumes are at least
[f(s)^(1/(d-1))+g(s)^(1/(d-1))]^(d-1)>=f(s)+g(s).
Integration gives
|A+B|>=(w_A+w_B)(a/w_A+a/w_B), which is exactly (9).
For d=2 the final section inequality is an equality algebraically;
for d>2 discarding its positive mixed terms may lose substantial mass.

## 5. A realized obstruction to closing the bound bundle, for every d>=3

In dimension d>=3 take centered rectangular boxes with side lengths

    A: (1,9/4,4/9,1,...,1),
    B: (1,4/9,9/4,1,...,1).

Both have volume a=1. Their actual Minkowski midpoint has side lengths
(1,97/72,97/72,1,...,1), so

    r=m/a=9409/5184<2.                                          (10)

In the first coordinate their exact widths are w_A=w_B=1. For d=3,
Gamma_3=27/64, and

    (1-Gamma_3)r=348133/331776>1.

Thus the residual lower bound (3) is zero. Meanwhile (8), even using
the TRUE widths rather than the weaker ratio bound (9), is only 1/32.
The paired mass needed by the uniform own-Grunbaum payment is

    Gamma_3(2-r)=959/12288,
    Gamma_3(2-r)-1/32=575/12288>0.                               (11)

This persists in every d>=3. Gamma_d decreases with d, because
t log(1+1/t) increases for t>0: its derivative is
log(1+1/t)-1/(t+1)>0, as is seen by integrating 1/(1+s) on [0,1/t].
Therefore (1-Gamma_d)r>1, and (3) is still zero. Also
W_d(1)<=1/32, whereas

    Gamma_d(2-r)>(1/3)(959/5184)>1/32,

using Gamma_d>1/e>1/3. The latter rational comparison is
32*959>3*5184. This proves exact failure of coverage by (3),(8),
even on realized bodies with exact widths, in every d>=3.

One may realize the potentially limiting middle volume k=2 by taking
K=(2/r)^(1/d)M about its common center zero. Then K contains M and
the three fibers are actual. This is STILL NOT a depth counterexample:
these boxes are centrally symmetric, and along the tested first
coordinate the paired endpoint mass is exactly 1 for every opposite
threshold pair. Moreover K is centrally symmetric of volume 2, so its
own cap at zero has volume 1 for every nonzero continuous normal;
this alone is greater than the required raw target 2Gamma_d. Thus the
displayed family explicitly satisfies OC. The weak universal
cap-homothety estimate merely fails
to record their flat section profiles. A proof beyond the window in
Section 1 must retain further geometric information; the estimates
(3),(8),(9) alone cannot supply the missing payment.
